problem: A client can compute an unlearning update, yet the server may identify or omit it during aggregation.
contribution: EFU binds compressed learning and unlearning updates to authorized encrypted aggregation, with auxiliary losses intended to reduce observable unlearning traces.
reading_guide: Read retained accuracy alongside forgotten-class or forgotten-task accuracy; neither metric establishes exact data erasure or universal undetectability.

diagram.title: One aggregation route for learning and unlearning
diagram.description: Clients independently choose learning or unlearning, then send encrypted centroids, mappings, and partial keys to one server; the decrypted aggregate returns to all clients.

stages.title: Choose local update
stages.detail: Learn retained data or compute an unlearning update; these are alternative client operations.

stages.title: Cluster and encrypt
stages.detail: Encrypt centroids under the round label; send mappings and partial functional keys alongside them.

stages.title: Expand encrypted weights
stages.detail: Use mappings to substitute encrypted centroids into each client model.

stages.title: Decrypt authorized aggregate
stages.detail: Combine partial keys, evaluate the agreed aggregate, and return the updated model to clients.

diagram.footnote: The aggregate returns to the clients each round. Enforcement concerns permitted decryption; successful deployment and exact forgetting are separate properties.

results.title: Class forgetting with retained utility
results.question: How does EFU compare with retraining and the unlearning methods it wraps?
results.context: CIFAR-10, ResNet-18, class-wise forgetting of 10% of classes; 10 clients, 1 unlearning client, 20% participation, 100 rounds. Accuracy in %; higher retain and lower forget are desired. Means of 3 runs; no dispersion reported.
results.interpretation: EFU is 2.39 percentage points below retraining on retained classes and has similar forgotten-class accuracy. Wrapping the baselines preserves broadly similar performance in this setting.
results.caveat: The PGD and FedOSD integrations also add MAS regularization. These are not pure encryption-only ablations; low forgotten accuracy alone does not prove removal of data influence.

results.title: Remove identity, retain gender
results.question: Can one task be suppressed while a shared backbone continues serving another?
results.context: LFW, ViT-B/32 with separate identity and gender heads; all 30 clients unlearn identity after round 50 of 100, with full participation. Test accuracy in %; higher gender and lower identity are desired. Means of 3 runs; no dispersion reported.
results.interpretation: EFU retains gender accuracy within 1.49 percentage points of retraining and reduces identity accuracy to 5.12%, close to the retraining reference of 4.71%.
results.caveat: This is a system-wide two-task LFW experiment, not evidence that arbitrary tasks or individual identities can always be removed without collateral loss.

evaluation.label: Data and models
evaluation.value: CIFAR-10, 30-identity LFW, and 62-class FEMNIST; pretrained ResNet-18 and ViT-B/32.

evaluation.label: Federated setting
evaluation.value: Flower simulations with Dirichlet concentration 0.1, 64 weight clusters, and a 256-bit DMCFE key; 1 local learning epoch and 5 unlearning epochs.

evaluation.label: Compared with
evaluation.value: Full retraining, SGA-EWC, PGD, FedOSD, and their EFU integrations; sample-, class-, and task-level experiments.

evaluation.label: Privacy evidence
evaluation.value: DMCFE-based proof sketches plus CIFAR-10 plots of aggregate parameter drift, local execution time, and message size; no tabulated detector accuracy.

limitations: The stated threat model trusts clients to generate keys and perform unlearning correctly. The decryption argument assumes the agreed function and no unauthorized alternative key; it does not force a server to continue training or deploy the returned model.

Encryption hides ciphertext contents under DMCFE assumptions. The server also sees mappings and aggregate outputs; the paper conditions update-type indistinguishability on indistinguishable function outputs, and its side-channel plots are not a general detection test.

The sample-wise rows report retained test accuracy but no forgotten-sample metric. Appendix C defines a prediction-gap proxy, but no numerical prediction-gap or membership-inference audit is reported.
The runtime comparison generates adversarial examples offline. Its measured local update time is not a complete accounting of unlearning preparation cost.
takeaways: Treat secure aggregation and the unlearning objective as separate components: the former constrains computation, while the latter determines behavioral forgetting.
Retention and forgetting must be assessed together, using retraining as a reference rather than treating low accuracy as an erasure certificate.
The empirical privacy evidence concerns specific parameter, timing, and communication signals on CIFAR-10.
